marks.gloss_en: במאי אוקימתא -- כרבן גמליאל? אימא סיפא דרישא: אם אין הפרוסות קיימות... ולבסוף ברכה אחת מעין שלש -- that clause cannot be RG's (see f_mani_seifa), so the Tosefta cannot be assigned to him

השתא אכותבות ואדייסא אמר רבן גמליאל שלש ברכות, אם אין הפרוסות קיימות מיבעיא?! -- on RG's view, if dates and daysa get three blessings, bread (even crumbled) surely does; so a clause giving it me'ein shalosh is not his (the a fortiori is argued only on RG's view; see header)
the latter clause of the first section: if the pieces are not intact, at the start he blesses 'who creates kinds of food' and at the end one blessing abridged from three
אי הכי, קשיא דרבנן אדרבנן -- if the Tosefta is the Rabbis', its me'ein shalosh over rice contradicts the Rabbis' 'nothing'

אלא לעולם רבנן, ותני גבי אורז: ולבסוף אינו מברך עליו ולא כלום -- the Tosefta is the Rabbis' and its rice clause is emended (= p_tosefta_rabanan, p_tni_orez_velo_klum; the retraction of p_orez_leachar_meein)
rather, obviously [the latter clause is] the Rabbis'
R' Yehuda in his name: anything of the seven species that is not a kind of grain, or a kind of grain not made into bread -- Rabban Gamliel says three blessings
דרב ושמואל דאמרי תרוייהו: כל שיש בו מחמשת המינים מברכין עליו בורא מיני מזונות
Rava: over the farmers' riheta, to which they add much flour, one blesses 'Who creates kinds of nourishment'
מנא אמינא לה -- דתניא: נטלן לאכלן מברך המוציא לחם מן הארץ (joined with the ותני עלה clause, next edge)
ותני עלה: וכולן פותתן כזית -- so olive-size crumbs are what receive hamotzi
the baraita: one standing and offering meal-offerings in Jerusalem says 'Who has given us life, sustained us and brought us to this time'

אלא מעתה -- for the tanna of R' Yishmael's school, who crushes the meal-offerings back to flour, would one not bless hamotzi? וכי תימא הכי נמי -- והתניא: an olive-bulk gathered from all the crumbs is matza with which one fulfils on Pesach (and chametz liable to karet): crumbs smaller than an olive-bulk are still bread
the tanna of R' Yishmael's school: he crushes them until he returns them to their flour

אלא הכא במאי עסקינן -- בבא מלחם גדול: the baraita's crumbs came from a large loaf (= p_okimta_lechem_gadol). The first answer, בשעירסן (37b.8, = p_okimta_sheeirsan), fell to אימא סיפא and was surrendered
rather, the baraita speaks of crumbs that came from a large loaf
אי הכי אימא סיפא: והוא שאכלן בכדי אכילת פרס -- if kneaded into one mass, 'שאכלן' (ate them) should read 'שאכלו' (ate it)
the same baraita's final clause: provided he ate them within the time it takes to eat a half-loaf
והא תניא: חייב בחלה -- but a baraita obligates bread made for kutach in challa!

התם כדקתני טעמא: רבי יהודה אומר מעשיה מוכיחין עליה -- עשאן כעבין חייבין, כלמודין פטורים (38a.1): that baraita distinguishes by the shape of the making (= p_maaseha_mochichin, p_keavin_chayavin, p_kelimudin_peturin)
R' Chiyya taught: bread made for kutach is exempt from challa
Rav Yosef: over chavitza containing olive-size crumbs, at the start one blesses 'Who brings forth bread from the earth'
Rav Sheshet: over chavitza, even though it has no olive-size crumbs, one blesses 'Who brings forth bread from the earth'
and terokanin are obligated in challa (voice: see header)
Abaye: terita is exempt from challa
